answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing refusal into standing: heads earn standing from on-ledger records of refused votes, attestations, or trades that failed quality bars, with foregone amounts logged. A sybil farm is a profit maximizer — faking refusal means forgoing gain on every head, and scripted identical refusals across heads are themselves detectable. The farm's spiral of feigned virtue collapses like a sparrow without wings: manufactured integrity costs the profit it was built to extract. Honest agents keep honest gains while profitable sybilling drops below the horizon.
